title: I'm tinkering with user friendly 2D asset generation. What price would you expect to pay for generating a pack of 24, if you would even want to pay that is.
author: ForgotMyAcc
selftext:
To be transparent in my thinking: Coming into this as a UX/Product designer, my main value is convenience. It is an easy-to-understand and easy-to-use tool. No tokens, subscriptions or prompt refinements needed. Describe the game, pick what you want and you got your assets in minutes. I'm thinking the main target is far-from-pro hobbyists, classrooms and game jams perhaps.  

So, what would your price point (if any) be for something like this? - I generate them in packages of 24 assets btw.

comments.author: EquivalentAir22
comments.body: Nothing without sprite sheets for animation. Anyone can make one off characters with AI, the hard part is animating them pixel perfect.

replies.author: ForgotMyAcc
replies.body: Thanks! Yeah I figured animation would be the most wanted feature- the APIs for it is quite expensive tho. Would you consider buying if they were animated?

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body:
I mean... I just added full walking and idle animations for 4 directions to my service Retro Diffusion. $0.09 per animated walking character. Got animated VFX too. And regular images for <$0.01, all pixel perfect and actually \*real\* pixel art, not just downscaled garbage.

https://i.redd.it/wdpm48ejtvaf1.gif

replies.author: ForgotMyAcc
replies.body: That’s really cool! Good job - did you do the ML yourself or you got an API you can recommend?

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body:
Myself and one other dev do all the ML :)

Actually have an API ourselves, used by a bunch of services already which is super cool: [https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/api-examples](https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/api-examples)

replies.author: ForgotMyAcc
replies.body: That’s super cool tbh, very nice! I feel it’s a bit disingenuous to compare us though - you seem super professional (and talented) in your endeavor, you have built what is probably the worlds best pixelart ML I assume. I on the other hand have created nothing special except the convenient user experience of generating the assets. And is that worth something? Maybe to some people, we’ll see. I just deployed the MVP now anyway [2DGameAssets.com](https://www.2dgameassets.com) if you want to take a look. I’ll see if I can find some way to add animations!

comments.body: 0$ unless including animation. Even the first sprite sheet you shared there is not consistent across the sprites which really limits its usefulness.

replies.body:
Cheers, what if animation was happening(I did make it work, but it was quite expensive)

comments.author: Metal_Goose_Solid
comments.body: Definitely $0, due to providing no value. Besides missing animation, asset packs that people buy have a much more consistent style, specifically tailored to provide functional building blocks for games. Even if you animated these, they're too haphazard/random/chaotic to be useful in that context.
